steps.title: The kernel ends at PID 1
steps.body:
The top row is the kernel with timestamps from this board's `dmesg`. Below it the same boot jobs run twice, once with Alpine's BusyBox init and once with Debian's systemd.

The kernel's work ends when it starts PID 1 (the first user-space process).

steps.title: 0.000 s: the kernel reads its inputs
steps.body: The kernel parses the DTB and the command line from U-Boot and reserves memory. Everything it learns about the hardware comes from the DTB.

steps.title: 0.006 s: four CPUs through BL31
steps.body: Linux starts the other cores with PSCI `CPU_ON`, an `smc` call answered by BL31. Without BL31 only one CPU would run.

steps.title: Drivers probe until 3.2 s
steps.body: Built-in drivers for UART, I2C, PMIC, eMMC, GPU, display and Ethernet initialise one after another. Most of the boot time is spent here.

steps.title: 3.26 s: wait for the SD card
steps.body: `rootwait` makes the kernel wait until `root=/dev/mmcblk1p1` appears, because the SD card may not be ready yet. Without it the kernel may try to mount the root before the card is ready and stop with a panic.

steps.title: 3.40 to 3.44 s: mount root and start init
steps.body: The ext4 partition p1 becomes `/` at 3.40 s, and at 3.44 s the kernel runs `/sbin/init`. From this moment user space is in charge.

steps.title: Alpine: one small file, run top to bottom
steps.body: BusyBox init reads `/etc/inittab` line by line. About 15 lines mount the filesystems, start `syslogd`, run `mdev` and `coldplug` and `hwclock`, and finish with a getty.

steps.title: Debian: units started in parallel
steps.body: systemd starts units by dependency, using `/etc/fstab`, `journald`, `udev`, `networkd`, `resolved` and ssh. The jobs are the same, but expressed as units instead of lines.

steps.title: Both end at a serial login
steps.body: The serial getty uses the `console=` value from the kernel command line, so the prompt appears on the same UART as the boot log. A getty on the screen is also started.
